transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Evan Park (CTO - Summit Digital), Lina Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Jon Miller (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Quick hosted API demo. Core topics: streaming responses, adjusting params for quality vs cost, retry strategies and idempotency, security/SOC2 and data retention. Next steps: pricing, security docs, PoC kickoff.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, i'll hand off to Diego in a sec to do a short walkthrough. Evan, Lina, Jon - thanks for making time.
00:08 Evan Park: Yeah thanks Maya. Quick context - we're evaluating a hosted provider to add chat summarization and a support-assist feature. Currently using OpenAI for prototyping, want something with better latency predictability and lower unit cost at scale.
00:22 Lina Gomez: And we have requirements around PII - we need SOC2 and ability to limit retention or use customer-managed KMS if possible. Also curious about streaming for faster UX and retries for idempotency.
00:34 Maya Chen: Totally. Diego, want to walk through the Hosted API chat basics - streaming, params, and how we handle retries?
00:40 Diego Ramos: Yep, thanks. So i'll share my screen — i'll paste a couple quick curl and SDK examples. First, a basic chat completion call: model param, messages array, temperature, top_p, max_tokens. Example: POST /v1/chat/completions with model=redwood-lite or redwood-qa. You get a sync response by default but to enable streaming you add stream=true and we push chunked events as tokens generate.
01:05 (slight interruption) Jon Miller: When you say chunked events, are you using SSE or web sockets?
01:10 Diego Ramos: Great q - we support chunked HTTP streaming via SSE-style events for browsers and SDKs, websockets via our SDK for lower overhead is coming, but for most clients SSE streaming works well. The transcript sometimes shows it as "stream=true" or the SDK streaming method.
01:26 Lina Gomez: How consistent is token ordering and partial outputs? We need to show progressive summarization in our UI without weird reordering.
01:33 Diego Ramos: You get deterministic token order from the model. There can be small edits if the model revises, but streaming is incremental; the Console also shows partials. We also have prefix and KV cache optimizations on the backend to reduce latency for repeated contexts — you might see it referred to in docs as K-V cash in older notes, haha.
01:52 Evan Park: Cool. Can you show an example of tuning temperature vs top_p for safe answers? Our legal team is worried about hallucination.
02:00 Diego Ramos: Sure. Temperature controls randomness; top_p is nucleus sampling. For deterministic outputs, set temperature=0 and top_p=0. Or keep top_p at 0.9 with lower temp for varied but safe outputs. For safety we also recommend prompt templates and instruction-finetuned models (we call out verified models in the catalog). We'll also run guardrails and allowlist/denylist in the Console for PII.
02:24 Maya Chen: Quick qualification - Evan/Lina, what's your target latency SLO for the summarization path?
02:28 Evan Park: Ideally sub-500ms for short replies (~200-300 tokens). For longer generations we can accept higher.
02:35 Diego Ramos: For that SLO we'd recommend a lower-latency model variant and enabling streaming so the UI can show tokens as they come. Also consider pinning to Dedicated for predictable throughput; hosted can still hit SLOs but with more variability depending on traffic.
02:51 Lina Gomez: That brings up data residency - we need EU data at rest for some customers. Do you offer region pinning on hosted?
02:58 Maya Chen: Yes, hosted supports regional endpoints; we can route EU traffic to EU regions. For stricter residency or on-prem we also offer Private deployments and VPC options. Diego, maybe touch on logs and retention?
03:10 Diego Ramos: Right — audit logs and request-level metadata are available in Console. By default Redwood retains logs for a configurable window; for enterprise we can set retention to match policy or disable retention and integrate with customer's log sinks. KMS integration for encryption-at-rest is supported; some customers use a bring-your-own-key flow.
03:29 Jon Miller: And network? Can we put the traffic through our NAT or do you need open endpoints?
03:34 Maya Chen: There are multiple patterns - customer can use TLS over public endpoints with IP allowlists, or for more secure setups we offer VPC peering and Private deployments with air-gapped options. We'll share the architecture notes in the security packet.
03:47 Evan Park: Great. Back to retries — in production we see transient 5xxs; what's your recommendation for idempotency and replays?
03:55 Diego Ramos: Two patterns: one, make the call idempotent by sending a client-side request_id header — that lets the runtime detect duplicates and avoid double-charging tokens. Two, use exponential backoff with jitter on 5xx and network errors. We recommend not retrying on certain 4xx errors like bad input. Our SDKs include a retry helper; sample pseudo: retry up to 3 attempts with backoff 500ms -> 1s -> 2s. Also we expose error codes in responses so you can programmatically decide.
04:25 Lina Gomez: If we stream and a retry happens mid-stream, do you resume or restart?
04:30 Diego Ramos: Good nuance — usually the client restarts the stream with the same request_id; our runtime will de-duplicate if the earlier attempt actually completed server-side. For partial writes the client should reconcile by checking final response states — we also provide a session token approach for long-running sessions. There's some complexity there but we've seen teams handle it with request_id + final-confirmation step.
04:52 Maya Chen: Any questions on cost tradeoffs — batching, token charges, or caching?
04:57 Evan Park: How is billing measured? Per-token both input and output? And does streaming affect cost?
05:03 Diego Ramos: Billing is per-token (input + output) for hosted API, streaming doesn't change billing, you pay for generated tokens. Batching and KV prefix caching can lower tokens sent and generated. For heavy workloads we also recommend quantized model variants to lower cost. Optimize (our cost/perf toolkit) can suggest batching sizes and quantization profiles.
05:25 Jon Miller: For benchmarking, can you run a PoC where we send our sample logs and see latency percentiles?
05:30 Diego Ramos: Absolutely — typical PoC plan: you provide sample dataset and target SLOs, we run a benchmark over a few runs and share p50/p90/p95, plus token cost estimates. We'll include a script and the SDK harness.
05:44 (audio crosstalk)
05:47 Lina Gomez: Security — can you confirm SOC 2 and SSO?
05:50 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II plus SAML/SSO and RBAC controls in Console. We'll attach the cert and the identity integration guide.
05:59 Evan Park: Any concerns about model drift or quality regression if you update model weights?
06:05 Diego Ramos: We have model versioning and rollouts in the Console — you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, and tie quality monitoring to evaluation prompt sets. Optimize will alert on regressions against your evaluation set.
06:20 Maya Chen: Ok, quick live demo: i’ll hand over to Diego to show a short SDK snippet with streaming and a retry hint.
06:27 Diego Ramos: (screen share) Example in node: const stream = client.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-chat-small', messages, stream: true, temperature: 0.2}); stream.on('data', chunk => { render(chunk.text) }); On error, use client.retries.withBackoff(requestId, ...) — pseudo. Note sometimes docs refer to the SDK method names slightly different; the Console code snippet is the canonical copy.
07:05 Lina Gomez: Looks good. Can you show stop sequences? We have multi-turn prompts and want to enforce end tokens.
07:12 Diego Ramos: Use stop: ["\n\n", "### END"] or explicit max_tokens. Also you can pass an output_schema to request structured JSON and we do best-effort extraction.
07:28 Evan Park: One more — what's the SLA for hosted?
07:32 Maya Chen: For hosted API we have a published uptime SLA for Pro/Enterprise tiers and Dedicated has stronger SLA for latency and throughput. We'll share the SLA doc in the follow-up.
07:42 Diego Ramos: Also want to note internal naming — some older docs say Redwooood or Redwoood (transcription of folks reading old notes) but catalog has verified labels.
07:50 (laugh)
07:54 Maya Chen: Ok last section - recap and actions. We heard: Summit Digital wants a hosted PoC to validate sub-500ms p50 for short summaries, SOC2 and KMS options required, and sample dataset to be provided. Next steps: we'll send pricing and security packet, Diego will prep PoC benchmark plan.
08:12 Evan Park: Sounds good. Thanks Maya and Diego.
08:16 Lina Gomez: Thanks team, will send dataset and SLO doc by Friday.
08:20 Maya Chen: Perfect — thanks all.

End of transcript.
